recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Name: Tippecanoe Herbs
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Offer Line: Use coupon code "innerverse" at checkout for a 10% discount!

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Bio: Michelle Lundquist describes herself as a folk herbalist, gardener and homemaker with a passion for plants and their ability to heal. She has studied and actively worked with herbs since 2013, drawing most of her knowledge from hands on experience and mentors of the wise woman tradition, and a do it yourself spirit runs through her work as she encourages people to take their wellbeing into their own hands. She hosted more than eighty episodes of The Healing Home podcast as a kitchen witch, homemaker and folk herbalist, and now co-hosts Symbolic Studies with her husband Mario Garza.
recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Name: Michelle Lundquist

recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Pillars, Swords, and the Seventh Gate", "body": "Mario opens the Libra discussion with the Justice card of the Marseille and Rider-Waite decks and the Adjustment card of Crowley's Thoth deck, reading the sign as a threshold that pierces the veil between the day side and the night side of the zodiac. He traces twin pillars as gateways, the sword that splits the one into two, and the scales as an image of the world axis. Gabe then lays out the minor decans of Crux, Lupus, and Corona Borealis, framing the wolf as the predator season that follows the harvest."}, {"title": "Lady Luck Inside the Word Justice", "body": "Chance proposes that the goddess Tyche, Lady Luck, hides inside the word justice, and frames Libra's scales as a law of luck in which winter fortune reflects how faithfully one followed the laws of nature through the year. Mario links the idea to dharma and to the Wheel of Fortune sitting just before Justice in the Rider-Waite sequence. The panel weighs decision as a cutting off, Libra's dry autumn air as vata season, and the hips as the body's balance point, with Michelle connecting tension held in the jaw to tension held in the hips."}, {"title": "A Golden Weave: Goldenrod and Goldenseal", "body": "Kyle introduces goldenrod through its name, Solidago, and his saying \"what was solid ago, be solid again,\" presenting it as stag medicine he associates with the kidneys and good standing. He argues that goldenrod is wrongly blamed for hay fever, since its heavy pollen travels by insect rather than wind. Michelle adds the bumblebee highway, Liberty Tea, and the goldenrod rubber in Edison's tires. With goldenseal, she shares how the bitter golden root became a personal teacher about her bond with food and digestion, and Kyle describes reaching for it in gallbladder work, linking it to courage."}, {"title": "Trees of Life: Argan and the Book Tree", "body": "Michelle presents argan, the iron tree of Morocco, as a drought-hardy source of a prized, softening oil she uses in soaps and facial oils. Kyle adds the traditional harvest in which goats climb the spiny branches, eat the fruit, and pass the nuts for women to clean and press, a weave of Aries grit and Venusian softness. Kyle then turns to beech, the book tree, tracing Buche and bok to the Ogham legend, and proposes that the fruit of the tree of knowledge was writing itself. Mario adds world axis symbolism, and Chance shares Celtic wishes written on fallen branches."}, {"title": "Circular Thoughts and Venusian Sensuality", "body": "Kyle describes a blind tea meditation in which students holding passionflower felt energy drop to their feet before they ever tasted it, and he casts the passionflower person as someone caught in circular, replaying thoughts at bedtime. He also questions the story that the flower was named for the Passion of Christ. Michelle presents ylang ylang, the flower of flowers, as a warm, comforting scent she blends for relaxation and self-esteem. Kyle reframes aphrodisiacs as communing with one's own sensuality rather than seducing others, and closes with carob, the weight and measure tree."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: What makes a plant Venusian? Kyle Denton (Tippecanoe Herbs), Michelle Lundquist, Mario Garza (Symbolic Studies) and Slick Dissident joined Chance Garton for the Libra installment of Astro Herbalism, reading goldenrod, argan, beech, goldenseal, passionflower and ylang ylang through astrology and the doctrine of signatures: a plant's shape, color, scent and growth as clues to its qualities and symbolic meaning.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In this remastered episode (originally aired October 11, 2023), audio has been improved and tangents trimmed, turning a rough livestream into a focused master class on Libra's themes of balance, beauty, relationship and discernment, the Justice and Adjustment cards in Tarot, the scales and their central axis, the turn from light into darkness, and the plants that carry these Venusian energies.
